description: The quantitative methods of epidemiology and the data systems behind public health: measures of disease frequency and association, study designs and bias, surveillance systems, outbreak investigation, compartmental SIR models, spatial epidemiology and the communication of public health data. Practised with browser-based simulations and public datasets, working through African cases such as malaria incidence, cholera and meningitis outbreaks and district surveillance reports.
modelledOn: Vynnycky and White, An Introduction to Infectious Disease Modelling
WHO and Africa CDC, Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR) Technical Guidelines
outcomes: Calculate and interpret incidence, prevalence, mortality rates and standardised rates and measures of association such as relative risk and odds ratios.
Choose an appropriate study design for a public health question and identify confounding, selection bias and information bias.
Describe how surveillance systems collect, analyse and act on data and evaluate a system's sensitivity, timeliness and representativeness.
Investigate an outbreak from case definition and line list through epidemic curves to control measures and a written report.
Build, simulate and fit SIR-type models and use them to estimate reproduction numbers and compare interventions.
Analyse and map spatial health data and communicate findings clearly and honestly to decision makers and the public.

units.title: Epidemiology and measures of disease frequency
topics: The epidemiological approach: person, place and time; the epidemiological triangle; natural history of disease
Counts, proportions, ratios and rates; incidence (risk and rate), prevalence and their relationship
Mortality and morbidity measures: crude, specific and case fatality rates; maternal and under-five mortality
Direct and indirect standardisation; population pyramids and denominators from census data
Burden of disease: DALYs and YLLs; malaria, HIV and TB burden in sub-Saharan Africa
Confidence intervals for rates and proportions

units.title: Measures of association and causation
topics: Risk difference, relative risk, odds ratio, attributable fraction
Two-by-two tables, chi-squared tests and confidence intervals
Causal inference: Bradford Hill considerations, counterfactuals, directed acyclic graphs
Screening and diagnostic tests: sensitivity, specificity, predictive values; rapid diagnostic tests for malaria

units.title: Study designs in epidemiology
topics: Descriptive studies: case reports, case series, ecological and cross-sectional studies; demographic and health surveys
Cohort studies: prospective and retrospective, follow-up, person-time
Case-control studies: selecting controls, matching, why the odds ratio is used
Randomised controlled trials: randomisation, blinding, intention to treat; community and cluster trials such as bed net trials
Bias and confounding: selection, information, recall; stratification, adjustment and effect modification
Sample size and power in outline; ethics of research with human participants

units.title: Surveillance systems
topics: Purposes and types of surveillance: passive, active, sentinel, syndromic, event-based, laboratory-based
Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response: priority diseases, case definitions, thresholds and weekly reporting
Notifiable diseases and the flow of reports from community to district to national level; DHIS2 for surveillance
Alert and epidemic thresholds; detecting aberrations with moving averages and statistical methods
Evaluating surveillance: sensitivity, positive predictive value, timeliness, completeness, representativeness
Community-based surveillance by community health volunteers; One Health and zoonotic surveillance

units.title: Outbreak investigation
topics: The steps of an outbreak investigation from verifying the outbreak to communicating findings
Case definitions (suspected, probable, confirmed), line lists and case finding
Epidemic curves: point source, continuing and propagated outbreaks; incubation periods
Analytical studies in an outbreak: attack rates and food-specific risk tables
Control measures, contact tracing and declaring an outbreak over
Simulated investigations: a cholera outbreak in a coastal community, a meningitis season in the northern belt, a Lassa fever cluster

units.title: Disease modelling: SIR models
topics: Compartmental models: SIR and SEIR differential equations; solving them numerically
The basic and effective reproduction numbers; herd immunity thresholds and vaccination coverage
Fitting models to incidence data; estimating growth rates and the reproduction number in real time
Stochastic models and early extinction; age structure and contact matrices
Modelling interventions: vaccination, isolation, treatment, vector control; malaria transmission in outline
Uncertainty and the limits of models; scenarios versus forecasts

units.title: Spatial epidemiology
topics: Spatial data: points, polygons, rasters, coordinate systems; geocoding health facilities and cases
Choropleth maps, rates by district, small-number problems and smoothing
Clusters and hotspots: Snow's cholera map, spatial autocorrelation, scan statistics
Access to care and catchment areas; mapping malaria risk with environmental data

units.title: Communicating public health data
topics: Choosing charts and tables for epidemiological data; honest axes, rates versus counts, uncertainty
Situation reports and epidemiological bulletins for district and national audiences
Risk communication with communities and the media; countering misinformation
Privacy and ethics in publishing health data; small-area disclosure risk and Data Protection Act 843
Project: an outbreak or surveillance analysis with a model, a map and a situation report

schedule.title: Measuring disease frequency
schedule.exercise: From a district's monthly malaria counts and population, calculate incidence risk, incidence rate, prevalence and case fatality rate, and describe the cases by person, place and time.

tasks.title: Compute incidence and prevalence from a provided table of 12 months of malaria cases and population, and plot both over time
Calculate crude, age-specific and case fatality rates from a district mortality table and rank the age groups by rate
Simulate a population followed for 5 years with a constant hazard and show that prevalence approximates incidence times average duration

schedule.title: Standardisation and burden of disease
schedule.exercise: Directly standardise the mortality rates of two regions to a standard population, explain why crude rates mislead, and compute DALYs for a small illustrative case set.

tasks.title: Draw population pyramids for two districts from census counts and describe how their age structures differ
Directly standardise the death rates of two regions to a standard population and compare crude and adjusted rate ratios
Compute exact confidence intervals for district malaria rates, plot them with a caterpillar chart, and flag districts significantly above the national rate

schedule.title: Measures of association and screening
schedule.exercise: From a two-by-two table of well water use and diarrhoea, calculate the risk ratio, odds ratio and attributable fraction with confidence intervals, and draw a DAG for one possible confounder.

tasks.title: Calculate risk difference, relative risk and odds ratio from a given two-by-two table and state in words what each means
Run a chi-squared test and compute the odds ratio with its 95 percent interval for three exposure tables and compare their significance
Compute predictive values of a malaria rapid test at 5, 20 and 50 percent prevalence and plot how positive predictive value changes

schedule.title: Descriptive, cohort and case-control studies
schedule.exercise: Choose the best observational design for three research questions (rare cancer, common exposure, quick survey), and justify each choice with strengths and biases.

tasks.title: Calculate person-time and incidence rates for exposed and unexposed groups in a cohort table and compute the rate ratio
Analyse a matched case-control dataset on a risk factor for typhoid, calculate the odds ratio, and interpret it in plain language
Analyse a cross-sectional survey extract by weighting to the sampling frame, tabulating prevalence by region, and flagging results with wide intervals

schedule.title: Trials, bias and confounding
schedule.exercise: Appraise a bed net cluster trial summary for bias and confounding, and compute the sample size needed per arm to detect a halving of incidence.

tasks.title: Randomly assign 40 participants to two arms with a seeded generator and check the arms are balanced on age and sex
Stratify a table by age to reveal confounding, compute crude and Mantel-Haenszel adjusted odds ratios, and explain the difference
Estimate by simulation the power of a two-arm trial for sample sizes 50 to 400 and plot power against sample size

schedule.title: Public health surveillance systems
schedule.exercise: Map the flow of a weekly cholera report from a community health post through the district to the national level, noting who acts on it and the delay at each step.

tasks.title: Classify ten patient presentations against the IDSR case definitions and decide which must be reported immediately versus weekly
Build a weekly reporting table of districts and diseases, aggregate it to regional and national totals with SQL, and find missing reports
Select the right surveillance type (passive, sentinel, event-based) for three outbreak scenarios and defend the choice against the rubric

schedule.title: Detecting aberrations and evaluating surveillance
schedule.exercise: Compute sensitivity and timeliness of a surveillance system from a validation table, and design a community health volunteer reporting scheme for a rural district.

tasks.title: Plot weekly counts with a 4-week moving average and mark the weeks that exceed the mean plus two standard deviations
Apply an epidemic threshold to 5 years of weekly meningitis counts and list which weeks and districts crossed the alert threshold
Evaluate a surveillance system against a gold-standard register by computing sensitivity, positive predictive value and median reporting delay

schedule.title: Outbreak investigation methods
schedule.exercise: Build a line list of 25 cases from narrative reports, apply a case definition, and draw an epidemic curve to infer the likely outbreak type.

tasks.title: Plot an epidemic curve from a 30-case line list by day of onset and say whether it looks point source or propagated
Apply suspected, probable and confirmed case definitions to a case list and decide who should be counted at each stage
Work the first five steps of an outbreak investigation scenario, choosing evidence to collect and decisions to make, scored against the rubric

schedule.title: Analysing and controlling outbreaks
schedule.exercise: Calculate food-specific attack rates for a wedding gastroenteritis outbreak, identify the likely vehicle, and propose control measures and criteria for declaring the outbreak over.

tasks.title: Calculate attack rates for each food at a function from a table and identify the food with the highest relative risk
Plan contact tracing in a Lassa fever cluster scenario, deciding which contacts to follow and when to release them
Investigate a simulated cholera outbreak in a coastal community from alert to control, weighing evidence and costs, and finish with a rubric score

schedule.title: Compartmental models
schedule.exercise: Write the SIR equations for a measles outbreak in a school, compute R0 from contact and recovery rates, and derive the vaccination coverage needed for herd immunity.

tasks.title: Solve an SIR model for a school with 500 pupils and plot susceptible, infectious and recovered curves over 60 days
Compute R0 and the herd immunity threshold for three beta values and show the effect on peak infections on one chart
Fit an SIR model to a 15-week incidence series by least squares, estimate beta and the reproduction number, and plot the fit with residuals

schedule.title: Stochastic models and intervention modelling
schedule.exercise: Compare a vaccination campaign at 60 and 80 percent coverage using your SEIR model, and write a short paragraph on what uncertainties limit its forecasts.

tasks.title: Add a vaccinated compartment to an SIR model and plot the epidemic at 0, 40 and 80 percent coverage on the same axes
Run 200 stochastic SIR simulations from one infectious case, and estimate the proportion that die out early versus produce a major outbreak
Build an SEIR model with isolation, vary three parameters over plausible ranges, and plot the spread of outcomes as scenario bands

schedule.title: Mapping health data
schedule.exercise: Explain why a choropleth of raw case counts misleads, redraw the plan using rates per 1000, and describe how to test whether a cluster of cases is real.

tasks.title: Plot district cholera rates per 100000 as a ranked bar chart and flag districts with fewer than 10 cases as unreliable
Plot the cases from Snow's cholera data against pump locations and identify the pump with the most surrounding cases
Compute distance from each village to the nearest clinic, estimate the share of the population beyond 5 km, and map the access gaps

schedule.title: Communicating epidemiological findings
schedule.exercise: Prepare a one-page situation report for a district health director from a given outbreak dataset, with one chart, one table, one map description, and a clear recommendation.

tasks.title: Redraw a misleading chart with a truncated axis and raw counts as an honest rates chart with uncertainty bars
Decide how to publish a village-level HIV table to avoid disclosing individuals, applying small-number suppression, and score against the rubric
Analyse a provided outbreak dataset end to end by building an epidemic curve, an SEIR fit and a district rate table, and summarise it
